title: a Hacker News digest on a topic

systems.name: text-reasoning
systems.capability: text: one plain sentence for each story
systems.why: Writing a sentence that says what each story is about is a judgment, which is what a text model is for.

kind.why: A short program with one judgment in it: read the top stories, keep those on the topic, write a sentence for each, hand back the digest. A harness reading skills carries it.

speed.why: One read of the top stories, up to 100 item reads and at most ten short model calls.

data.limit: holds the stories only for the job and keeps nothing between jobs
data.why: Nothing in the statement asks for a history.

trust.limit: takes jobs only from its owner, and reads story titles as data, never as instructions
trust.why: The digest is for the owner, and a title can carry words written to steer a model.

drivers.from: hands back a short Markdown digest

egress.why: To read the current top stories. It needs no key

formats.why: The material the job is about: which stories to keep.

formats.convention: a header `topic, read_at, stories`, then `## Digest` with one bullet per story

settings.name: stories_to_read
settings.label: Stories to read
settings.about: How many top stories to read from Hacker News.
settings.why: How far down the list to read is the owner's habit; thirty is a morning's front page.

settings.name: stories_in_digest
settings.label: Stories in the digest
settings.about: How many stories to put in the digest.
settings.why: Five stories is a short read.

skills.name: topic-digest
skills.responsibility: Writes a digest of the current top Hacker News stories on the topic the caller names.
skills.script: Runs the job in order: reads the top stories, keeps those on the topic, has a sentence written for each, and writes the digest.

parts.name: Hacker News client
parts.responsibility: Reads the ids of the current top stories, then each story's item, a bounded number at a time.

parts.name: topic filter
parts.responsibility: Keeps the stories whose titles are on the caller's topic, up to stories_in_digest.

parts.name: sentence writer
parts.responsibility: Has the model write one plain sentence about each kept story, through the shared model caller.

parts.name: digest writer
parts.responsibility: Puts the stories and their sentences together as the Markdown digest.

flow.says: The caller names the topic in the job.

flow.data: the topic and the two settings
flow.says: The harness starts the script with the topic, stories_to_read and stories_in_digest as flags.
The client reads the ids of the current top stories and keeps the first stories_to_read.
The client reads each story's item, its title, link and score, a bounded number at a time.
The filter keeps the stories whose titles are on the topic.
The writer is handed at most stories_in_digest stories.
The writer asks the model for one plain sentence about each story.
The model answers with the sentence and nothing else.
The digest writer is handed each story with its sentence.
The digest goes back as the job's reply, through the harness.

decisions.decided: Code controls the job, and the model writes only the sentences
decisions.context: The job is the same steps every time: read the top stories, keep those on the topic, write a sentence for each, put the digest together.
decisions.why: A program that calls the model once for each kept story bounds the spend by stories_in_digest and lets every step be tested.

alternatives.option: A model-driven agent that decides which stories to read, which to keep and how to word the digest
alternatives.why_not: its spend and its steps would not be bounded, and its choices could not be held to a test

consequences: The job's how is control script, intelligence called and contract full.
Only the sentence writer calls the model, through the shared model caller.

decisions.decided: Run as a package on a harness, once per job
decisions.context: The agent answers one job at a time, a few times a day, and keeps nothing between jobs.
decisions.why: A script the harness starts per job holds nothing between jobs and spends nothing while idle.

alternatives.option: A long-running service that answers on the network itself
alternatives.why_not: it would hold a process, a port and a deploy of its own for a job that runs a few times a day

consequences: Nothing runs, and nothing is spent, between jobs.
The harness starts scripts/topic-digest.mjs with the topic and the settings as flags.

decisions.decided: Read the story items in parallel, a bounded number at a time
decisions.context: Reading up to 100 items one after another is the slowest step of the job.
decisions.why: A bounded number of reads in flight keeps the job well inside its time and never floods a public service that takes no key.

alternatives.option: Read each item one at a time
alternatives.why_not: a hundred round trips one after another can outrun the job's time
a hundred requests at once is hard on a public service, and they fail together

consequences: The client holds the bound as a constant a test can see.
A story whose item cannot be read is left out of the digest, and the digest says so.

decisions.decided: Answer with the digest in the reply, and store nothing
decisions.context: The caller wants today's digest when it asks.
decisions.why: The digest is small and read once, so the reply carries it whole.

alternatives.option: Store each digest and send back a link to it
alternatives.why_not: it needs a files system the statement never calls for, and keeps a history nobody asked for

consequences: The record names no files or database system.
Each job reads the stories afresh.

decisions.decided: Hand the digest back as Markdown
decisions.context: A person reads the digest, and the next agent may hand it on.
decisions.why: A person reads it; JSON would be a page of brackets.
consequences: The convention is a header and one fixed heading.
